items.title: The manufacturing data gap holding back physical AI
items.summary: Manufacturers looking to deploy autonomous robots must close gaps in industrial data collection, interoperability, and quality feedback to enable reliable decision-making and improve production efficiency. The post The manufacturing data gap holding back physical AI appeared first on The Robot Report .

items.title: Medtronic’s Hugo surgical robot ready for bigger operation
items.summary: Globally, the Hugo surgical system is on track to surpass 50,000 cumulative procedures by the end of Medtronic's fiscal year. The post Medtronic’s Hugo surgical robot ready for bigger operation appeared first on The Robot Report .

items.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
items.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions.

items.title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
items.summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates.

items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored.

items.title: What Must a Model Tell a Planner? Outcome Interfaces for Risk-Aware Planning After Robot Damage
items.summary: When a robot is damaged, it must decide which routes it can still afford, and the amount of risk it may accept can change from one mission to the next. We argue that whether a learned model helps such a robot depends on its decision interface, that is, on what the model hands to the planner.

items.title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing
items.summary: Autonomous racing requires an accurate vehicle dynamics model near the limits of handling, yet a mismatch between the nominal and actual dynamics inevitably remains.

items.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints.

items.title: MassRobotics launching marine robotics facility on Boston Harbor
items.summary: MassRobotics plans to open the marine-focused facility in early 2028, with programming starting throughout 2027. The post MassRobotics launching marine robotics facility on Boston Harbor appeared first on The Robot Report .

items.title: Humanoid robots for safety-critical electrical switching: A perception-informed runtime constraint filter
items.summary: Humanoid robots can reduce personnel exposure in electrical switching, but safe control is challenging because the tool must reach a target switch next to similar devices, where an imprecise operator command can contact a non-target switch. This study proposes a runtime safety filter that checks each operator command during virtual-reality teleoperation of a humanoid robot.

items.title: BRINA: Bottom-Referenced Inertial Navigation with AKAZE, a Sonar SLAM for Autonomous Marine Vehicles
items.summary: Forward-looking sonar (FLS) provides reliable underwater perception where optical sensing is limited, but its use for navigation is hindered by the unobserved elevation of each return. As a result, motion estimated directly from sonar images suffers from an unknown metric scale that is commonly resolved using a Doppler velocity log (DVL).

items.title: Generalist Action Critic: Harnessing Frontier Models in Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Frontier models have demonstrated remarkable general-purpose reasoning capabilities, opening new possibilities for intelligent decision making in the physical world. In autonomous driving, many recent approaches seek to leverage these capabilities through additional adaptation for action output, particularly in scenarios where existing models underperform.

items.title: EvoTER: Evolving Embodied Agents via Tool-Use Experience and Reflection
items.summary: Long-horizon embodied tasks require agents to ground instructions in changing observations, coordinate heterogeneous tools, and recover from failures that can propagate through downstream operations. Although existing LLM-based agents retain experience and refine reusable skills, successful local repairs do not by themselves establish complete-task gains over the current shared procedure library.

items.title: An Autonomous Adaptive Learning System for Robotic Grasping in the Circular Factory
items.summary: Linear manufacturing typically operates in highly structured settings with standardized objects, allowing robots to execute pre-programmed motions based on precise models. In contrast, circular manufacturing involves dynamic and less controlled environments, where product components can vary due to appearance and physical changes across different product generations.

items.title: To Own or Not to Own? Endogenous Ownership in Peer-to-Peer Sharing of Private Autonomous Vehicles
items.summary: Autonomous driving allows private owners to release their vehicles to an on-demand platform and earn income when they do not need them. This possibility changes vehicle acquisition incentives, as rental income can encourage purchases, while access to shared vehicles can reduce the need for personal ownership.

items.title: Dynamics of a spherical ferromagnet on a non-conducting incline in an external magnetic field
items.summary: Magnetic particles of various shapes and sizes are used in biomedical applications, robotics, nanomagnetism, electrotechnology, and education. Yet despite years of study, a theoretical description of the rolling motion of a solid magnetic sphere still eludes us.

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters.

items.title: Trust What Repeats: Capped World-Model Policy Gradients for Humanoid Motion Tracking
items.summary: Training a humanoid motion tracker by backpropagating imagined returns through a learned world model is fast, because the model gives a first-order policy gradient. We ask how much of that gradient holds in the simulator.

items.title: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models
items.summary: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can improve pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies through imagined experiences. However, existing VLA-MBRL methods primarily rely on large-scale image or video generation world models, incurring large computational overhead.

items.title: SOAR: Training-Free Rank-Consistent Rollout Compression for Latent World Model Planning
items.summary: Latent world models plan by rolling out hundreds of candidate action sequences through a transformer predictor, so a single decision can take tens of seconds. Existing accelerations prune spatial tokens as in vision-language models, yet a sampling-based planner uses predicted costs only to rank candidates, so a rollout can be compressed freely as long as the ranking survives.

items.title: Seeing Is Not Steering: Where Verifiable Reasoning Can Enter an End-to-End Driving Planner
items.summary: Driving models that reason may describe a hazard correctly while choosing their path for other reasons. We study where scene reasoning can enter an end-to-end planner so its influence can be checked. We freeze Drive-JEPA and use a fine-tuned vision-language model to state scene facts. Although fine-tuning improves fact accuracy, the two learned components we test show no detectable benefit from reading them.

items.title: Instant-LIVO: Efficient LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry with Compact Geometry and a Bounded Single-Reference-Frame Map
items.summary: LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (LIVO) is a fundamental technology for autonomous systems; however, deployment on resource-constrained platforms remains challenging due to physical limitations. This paper presents Instant-LIVO, a tightly coupled, high-speed, real-time LIVO system.

items.title: Synthesizing Expressive Human-Object Interactions via Test-time Latent Adaptation
items.summary: When interacting with objects of unknown physical properties, humans sometimes probe, over-exert, stagger, and adjust through iterative adaptation instead of succeeding immediately. We argue that this process is an expressive but largely overlooked aspect of human-object interaction in motion synthesis.

items.title: Planar Formation Control with Minimal Sensing and No Common Orientation: An Almost-Global Result
items.summary: Formation control based on geometric constraints often requires either rigid interaction graphs or a common orientation reference. This paper investigates whether a prescribed planar formation can instead be achieved using only $N-1$ pairwise interactions while preserving global rotational freedom.

items.title: Adesktop learning factory for smart and resilient manufacturing based on digital twin and AI
items.summary: Learning factories have been increasingly applied in engineering research and education. In this paper, we develop a small-scale, low-cost, fully open-sourced learning factory that leverages AI and digital twins to demonstrate smart and resilient manufacturing. The learning factory consists of an AGV, three robots, two conveyors and their digital twins.

items.title: S-BFM: A Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control from Sparse Spatiotemporal Goals
items.summary: General-purpose whole-body trackers can execute diverse humanoid motions, but they require dense reference trajectories. However, tasks usually specify only where, in which posture, and when the robot should arrive, leaving the motion in between to a separate planner.

items.title: Where Delay Compensation Belongs in a Decentralized Mean-Field-Game Swarm with a Control-Barrier Safety Filter
items.summary: Large robot teams are often run as a plan-then-execute stack. We study a decentralized instance for drone swarms, a mean-field-game (MFG) routing field with a per-agent control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filter, when communication is limited by a shared TDMA channel.

items.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
items.summary: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required.

items.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
items.summary: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample.

items.title: Fault-Geometry-Aware Control Allocation for Emergency Quadrotor Landing under Single-Motor Loss of Effectiveness
items.summary: Partial single-motor loss of effectiveness (LoE) changes the remaining control-authority geometry of a quadrotor and can change which control allocator performs best during emergency landing.

items.summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on vision-language backbones, tying policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control.

items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to train robust, adaptable systems across healthcare, e-commerce, and robotics. items.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Recent years have witnessed an explosive trend of scaling ego-centric human videos for robot manipulation, yet it remains unclear which data actually benefits dexterous manipulation. We present SiMDex, a similarity-based data mining framework that casts human data selection for VLA post-training in dexterous manipulation as a recommendation problem.
